insights.title: FY26 bank credit growth hits 16.1%, up 5.1 points on FY25
insights.body: Bank credit grew 11.0% in the year ending March 2025 and 16.1% in the year ending March 2026, a 5.1 point acceleration. The full-year growth rate stepped up from 11.0% in FY25 to 16.1% in FY26, a 5.1 point increase.
insights.implication: The 5.1 point jump from FY25 to FY26 remains the largest full-year acceleration in this dataset, a reading unchanged since July's evaluation.

inferences: Bank credit grew 11.0% in FY25 and 16.1% in FY26.
That is a 5.1 point step-up in the full-year pace.
This is an annual metric set at the March year-end; it does not move month to month.

insights.title: FY26 net credit add holds at ₹29.6L Cr, highest on record
insights.body: Banks deployed ₹29.6L Cr of net new credit in FY26, the highest annual addition in this window. This figure has stayed flat at ₹29.6L Cr across all 25 periods shown, since it reflects the full-year tally locked at the March 2026 year-end.
insights.implication: The ₹29.6L Cr FY26 addition stays the largest annual deployment on record, with the book continuing to grow past year-end into August.

inferences: FY26 net new credit stands at ₹29.6L Cr, unchanged across all 25 periods shown.
It is an annual figure fixed at the March 2026 year-end, so it does not move period to period.
It remains the largest annual addition in this dataset.

insights.title: Bank credit growth eases to 19.08% YoY after four-month climb
insights.body: Bank credit grew 19.08% year-on-year in August 2026. Growth slipped 0.25 points from July's 19.33% to 19.08%, the first pause after four straight months of acceleration from April's 16.0%.
insights.implication: The 0.25 point dip is the first break in four months of acceleration, but at 19.08% growth is still well above the upper range of this window, so this reads as a pause rather than a reversal.

inferences: August's YoY growth is 19.08%, down from 19.33% in July.
That ends a four-month run of acceleration that took growth from 16.0% in April to 19.33% in July.
The reading still sits in the upper range of this 17-period window, above the 16.9% mark that otherwise bounds that range.

insights.title: Food credit falls to ₹1.12L Cr, third straight monthly drop
insights.body: Food credit outstanding stood at ₹1.12L Cr in August 2026, down ₹0.06L Cr from July. Volume declined ₹0.06L Cr period-on-period (₹1.18L Cr → ₹1.12L Cr), the third consecutive monthly decline since the May 2026 all-time high of ₹1.37L Cr.
insights.implication: Three consecutive monthly declines from the May peak of ₹1.37L Cr mark the first sustained pullback in this series, even though the ₹1.12L Cr level is still in the upper range of this window.

inferences: Food credit fell to ₹1.12L Cr in August, down from ₹1.18L Cr in July.
That is the third straight monthly drop since the ₹1.37L Cr peak in May 2026.
Despite the pullback, the level remains in the upper range of this 25-period window.

insights.title: Food credit YoY growth leaps to 145.8%, a new series high
insights.body: Food credit grew 145.81% year-on-year in August 2026, the highest rate in this 17-period window. Growth jumped 37.9 points (107.9% → 145.8%), surpassing the prior high of 139.4% set in March 2026.
insights.implication: The 37.9 point jump to 145.8% is the sharpest acceleration in this dataset, pushing food credit YoY growth to a new high above the prior 139.4% peak from March 2026.

inferences: Food credit YoY growth hit 145.8% in August, up from 107.9% in July — a 37.9 point jump.
That is above the previous high of 139.4% recorded in March 2026, making this a fresh high for the series.
This is a YoY rate, so the jump reflects growth measured against August 2025's base, not a change within this period alone.

insights.title: Non-food credit hits ₹222.8L Cr, re-accelerating after July
insights.body: Non-food credit outstanding reached ₹222.8L Cr in August 2026, the highest level on record. Volume climbed ₹3.2L Cr period-on-period (₹219.6L Cr → ₹222.8L Cr), a bigger gain than July's ₹1.6L Cr addition, continuing the climb from ₹178.1L Cr in January 2025.
insights.implication: August's ₹3.2L Cr gain reverses July's slowdown in non-food credit, the same re-acceleration pattern seen in total bank credit this period.

inferences: Non-food credit outstanding hit ₹222.8L Cr in August, up from ₹219.6L Cr in July.
The ₹3.2L Cr add is roughly double July's ₹1.6L Cr gain, though still below June's record ₹4.2L Cr addition.
The series remains at or near its 25-period maximum, extending the climb from ₹178.1L Cr in January 2025.

insights.title: Non-food credit growth slips to 18.77% from 19.06%
insights.body: Non-food credit grew 18.77% year-on-year in August 2026, down from 19.06% the prior period. Growth eased 0.29 points (19.06% → 18.77%), the first pullback after rising for three straight months from April's 15.8% to July's 19.1%.
insights.implication: August's dip to 18.77% is the first deceleration since the climb began in April, but non-food credit is still growing faster than in most of the last 17 periods, above the 16.6% upper-range mark.

inferences: Non-food credit grew 18.77% year-on-year in August 2026, down from 19.06% the prior period — a pullback of 0.29 points.
That breaks a three-month climb: growth had risen from 15.8% in April 2026 to 19.1% in July 2026.
Even after easing, 18.77% stays above the 16.6% mark that defines the top of this 17-period window's typical range.
The first deceleration since April's trough shows the recent run-up has lost a little pace, while growth stays at an elevated level.

gaps.title: Bank credit hits record ₹223.9L Cr, re-accelerating in August
gaps.body: Total bank credit outstanding reached ₹223.9L Cr in August 2026, the highest level on record. Volume climbed ₹3.1L Cr period-on-period (₹220.8L Cr → ₹223.9L Cr), a bigger gain than July's ₹1.5L Cr addition, continuing the climb from ₹178.7L Cr in January 2025.
gaps.implication: August's ₹3.1L Cr gain reverses July's slowdown, with the book still expanding without a single monthly contraction since January 2025.

inferences: Bank credit outstanding hit ₹223.9L Cr in August 2026, up from ₹220.8L Cr in July.
The ₹3.1L Cr add is more than double July's ₹1.5L Cr gain, though still below June's record ₹4.1L Cr addition.
The series remains at or near its 25-period maximum, with the book growing every month since January 2025's ₹178.7L Cr.

insights.title: Agriculture share falls to 12.23% — new low in range
insights.body: Agriculture's share of total bank credit stands at 12.23% in Aug 2026. Share declined 0.09pp from 12.33% to 12.23%, moving further below the 25th percentile of 12.4% to a new low in this 25-period window.
insights.implication: At 12.23%, agriculture's share of total credit is at or near the lowest point in this 25-period window, continuing a multi-year drift down from 12.8% readings in 2024.

inferences: Agriculture's share fell to 12.23% in Aug 2026, down from 12.33% the prior period.

The series shows the share drifting down from readings as high as 12.8% in 2024 to 12.2-12.3% in recent months.
Agriculture's slice of the overall credit book keeps narrowing even as the sector itself keeps growing.

insights.title: Agriculture credit YoY hits 17.22% — fresh high in window
insights.body: Agriculture credit grew 17.22% YoY in Aug 2026. Growth accelerated 0.25pp from 16.98% to 17.22%, extending above the prior high and the 75th percentile of 15.3%.
insights.implication: Agriculture credit's 17.22% YoY rate is the highest point in this 17-period series, part of a climb from 6.8% in Jun 2025 that has kept setting new highs period after period.

inferences: Agriculture credit grew 17.22% YoY in Aug 2026, up from 16.98% the prior period.
This is at or near the maximum of its 17-period range, well above the 75th percentile of 15.3%.
The series shows growth climbing steadily from a trough of 6.8% in Jun 2025 to 17.2% now.
The sector's YoY pace keeps setting new highs in this window.

insights.title: Industry FY growth jumps 8.2% to 15.0% — up 6.8 points
insights.body: Industry credit's full-year growth rose from 8.2% in FY25 to 15.0% in FY26. FY growth stepped up 8.2% → 15.0%, a 6.8-point acceleration recorded at the Mar 2026 year-end.
insights.implication: The 6.8-point jump from 8.2% to 15.0% between FY25 and FY26 nearly doubled industry credit's full-year growth rate at the Mar 2026 year-end.

inferences: Industry credit grew 8.2% in FY25 and 15.0% in FY26 — a 6.8-point step-up.
This is an annual metric set once at the March year-end, not a monthly reading.
The FY26 rate is nearly double the FY25 rate.

insights.title: Industry share drops to 21.53%, now below its range floor
insights.body: Industry's share of total bank credit fell to 21.53% in Aug 2026. Share declined 0.33pp from 21.86% to 21.53%, moving from above the 75th percentile of 22.3% to below the 25th percentile of 21.6% in one period.
insights.implication: Industry's share swung from above the 75th percentile to below the 25th percentile in a single period, falling to 21.53% — close to the 21.5% low seen earlier in 2026.

inferences: Industry's share fell to 21.53% in Aug 2026, down 0.33pp from 21.86% the prior period.
The reading moved from above the 75th percentile (22.3%) to below the 25th percentile (21.6%) in a single period.
The 25-period series shows a low of 21.5% (seen in Jan-Apr 2026) and a high of 22.8% (Dec 2023); the current reading sits near that low.
Industry's hold on a larger slice of the book, visible in recent months, pulled back to near the bottom of this range.

insights.title: Industry credit YoY eases to 18.23% from 19.95%
insights.body: Industry credit grew 18.23% YoY in Aug 2026. Growth decelerated 1.72pp from 19.95% the prior period, though it stays above the 75th percentile of 16.3% in this 17-period window.
insights.implication: Industry credit growth eased to 18.23% from 19.95%, the first step back after a climb from 6.3% in Jun 2025 to 20.0% in Jul 2026 — it still sits above the 75th percentile of 16.3%.

inferences: Industry credit grew 18.23% YoY in Aug 2026, down 1.72pp from 19.95% the prior period.
The reading remains above the 75th percentile of 16.3%, so growth stays in the upper part of its range despite the pullback.
The series shows growth climbing from 6.3% in Jun 2025 to 20.0% in Jul 2026 before this step-down.
The multi-period climb in industry credit growth paused in Aug 2026.

insights.title: Personal Loans is the biggest slice of the parent category at 32.7%
insights.body: Personal Loans holds the largest share of the parent category at 32.7%, Services 28.3%; Agriculture and Allied Activities is the smallest at 12.2%. These are size shares, not growth rates. Top three hold 82.5% of the parent category, spread 20.5 percentage points.
insights.implication: Composition, not momentum: Personal Loans carries the most weight of the parent category. Concentration means the big blocks drive the category — watch them first.

inferences: Personal Loans is the largest block at 32.7% of the parent category.
Agriculture and Allied Activities is the smallest at 12.2% — a 20.5 percentage points spread across 4 sub-categories.
The top three hold 82.5% of the parent category — concentrated mix.

insights.title: Services growing fastest at 24.3%; Personal Loans slowest at 16.9%
insights.body: Services leads YoY growth at 24.3%, Industry at 18.2%; Personal Loans is slowest at 16.9%. 4 of 4 categories growing, spread 7.4 percentage points.
insights.implication: Services is the fastest at 24.3% and the largest block at 28.1% of the category — pace and weight point the same way. Most of the category is growing.

inferences: Services is the standout at 24.3% YoY.
Personal Loans is the weakest at 16.9% — a spread of 7.4 percentage points across 4 categories.
4 of 4 categories are growing — broad-based momentum.

insights.title: Personal loans hold steady at 32.71% of total credit
insights.body: Personal loans account for 32.71% of total bank credit in Aug 2026. Share was unchanged at 32.71% from the prior period, sitting near the median of its 32.6%–32.9% range over 25 periods.
insights.implication: Personal loans' share is steady at 32.71%, sitting near the middle of its 25-period range — the segment is neither gaining nor losing ground in the overall credit mix this period.

inferences: Personal loans held 32.71% of total bank credit in Aug 2026, unchanged from the prior period's 32.71%.
That keeps the share within the 32.6%–32.9% range seen across the past 25 periods, near the median.
A flat reading like this, within half a point, counts as noise rather than a shift in the credit mix.

insights.title: Personal loans YoY growth climbs to 16.92%, a new high
insights.body: Personal loans credit grew 16.92% year-on-year in Aug 2026. Growth accelerated from 16.23% to 16.92%, and is now at or near the highest reading in this 17-period series (12.0% in Dec 2024 → 16.92% now).
insights.implication: Personal loans growth at 16.92% is at or near its highest level across this 17-period dataset, continuing an acceleration that started at 12.0% back in Dec 2024.

inferences: Personal loans grew 16.92% YoY in Aug 2026, up from 16.23% the prior period.
The gain extends a climb that began at 12.0% in Dec 2024, placing growth at or near the top of this 17-period range.
Sustained acceleration across multiple periods points to broadening momentum in personal loans rather than a one-off reading.

insights.title: Services credit grew 12% in FY25, 19% in FY26, a 7-point step-up
insights.body: Services credit grew 12.0% in the year ending Mar 2025 and 19.0% in the year ending Mar 2026. Full-year growth stepped up from 12.0% to 19.0%, a 7.0-point acceleration measured at the Mar 2026 year-end.
insights.implication: Services credit's full-year growth stepped up by 7.0 points between FY25 and FY26 (12.0% → 19.0%), a sizeable move for an annual metric that only changes once a year.

inferences: Services credit grew 12.0% in FY25 and 19.0% in FY26, a 7.0-point acceleration.

insights.title: Services share ticks up to 28.27%, stays in upper range
insights.body: Services account for 28.27% of total bank credit in Aug 2026. Share edged up from 28.22% to 28.27%, staying above the upper end of its typical 27.5%–28.2% band seen across the past 25 periods.
insights.implication: Services' share at 28.27% stays in the upper part of its 25-period range, little changed from last period's 28.22% — the segment is holding its elevated position rather than extending or giving it back.

inferences: Services held 28.27% of total credit in Aug 2026, up from 28.22% the prior period.
That keeps the share above the upper end of its 25-period range (27.5%–28.2%), where it has sat since peaking in Mar 2026 at 28.5%.
A move of this size is within the noise band for a share reading, not a structural shift.

insights.title: Services credit growth hits 24.35% — fastest in 17 periods
insights.body: Services credit grew 24.35% year-on-year in Aug 2026. Growth accelerated again, from 22.94% last period to 24.35% now — a 1.4-point gain. Over the past year it moved 12.0% (Mar 2025) → 19.0% (Mar 2026) → 22.9% (Jul 2026) → 24.3% (Aug 2026).
insights.implication: Services credit has broken its own record for a fourth straight period, reaching 24.35% — the strongest reading in this 17-period window. The 1.4-point acceleration from 22.94% confirms the trend is still strengthening, not plateauing, with growth now roughly double the 12.0% rate seen in Mar 2025.

inferences: Services credit grew 24.35% year-on-year in Aug 2026, up from 22.94% in Jul 2026 — a gain of 1.4 points.
This is the fourth consecutive period of acceleration, and the current 24.35% reading sits at or near the highest level seen in this 17-period window.
Growth has moved from 12.0% in Mar 2025 to 24.35% now, pointing to broad-based momentum in services credit rather than a short-lived spike.

insights.title: Services took 35.0% of all new bank credit in the past year
insights.body: Of the bank credit added over the past twelve months, Services took 35.0% — the largest share of the new money — growing 24.3% a year and accelerating (+1.40 pp). The rest went to Personal Loans 30.0%; Industry 21.0%; Agriculture and Allied Activities 11.4%. Industry took 21.0% while growing 18.2% a year and slowing (-1.72 pp) — a smaller slice of a faster-growing total, not a retreat.
insights.implication: Shares of new lending move far faster than shares of the book, so this is the earlier read of the two. It says where the money went, not why — and a falling share alongside rising growth means the others grew faster, not that this one shrank.

inferences: Every sector's bank credit is compared with the same month a year earlier, and each one's share of the total increase is taken.
Services accounts for 35.0% of the increase.
All sectors moved the same way this window, so the shares of the net increase are bounded and sum to a hundred.

gaps.implication: With breadth steady at 4 of 4 for most of this 25-period window, the credit expansion stays broad-based across agriculture, industry, services and retail, with no sector lagging into contraction.

inferences: Breadth stayed at 4 of 4 main sectors with positive YoY growth in August 2026, unchanged from the prior period.

No sector has slipped into contraction through this stretch, keeping the expansion spread across all four rather than concentrated in one or two.

insights.title: Large corporate credit growth cools to 14.88%, down from 17.69% peak

inferences: Large corporate credit grew 14.88% YoY in Aug 2026, down 2.81 points from a 17.69% peak the prior period.

Even after the pullback, 14.88% sits above the top quartile of this 17-period range, where p75 is 12.2%.

insights.title: Medium enterprises share climbs to 10.2% — fresh high
insights.body: Medium enterprises accounted for 10.19% of industry credit in Aug 2026, up from 9.99% in Jul 2026. Share rose from 9.99% to 10.19%, a +0.20pp gain that extends the climb from 8.1% in Dec 2023 and holds the segment at or near the maximum of this 25-period window (p75 9.7%).

insights.implication: Medium enterprise credit growth has extended its run to a third straight period of gains, reaching 31.78% — the fastest pace recorded in this 17-period series.

insights.title: Infrastructure took 19.0% of all new industry credit in the past year
insights.body: Of the industry credit added over the past twelve months, Infrastructure took 19.0% — the largest share of the new money — growing 10.2% a year and steady (-0.04 pp). The rest went to All Engineering 11.7%; Basic Metal and Metal Product 11.5%; Other Industries (not broken down) 9.6%; Chemicals and Chemical Products 8.7%; Food Processing 6.2%; Textiles 6.1%; Vehicles, Vehicle Parts and Transport Equipment 5.8%; Construction 5.3%; Gems and Jewellery 5.0%; Petroleum, Coal Products and Nuclear Fuels 3.5%; Rubber, Plastic and their Products 2.4%; Mining and Quarrying 1.3%; Cement and Cement Products 1.2%; Paper and Paper Products 1.1%; Wood and Wood Products 0.7%; Glass and Glassware 0.5%; Beverage and Tobacco 0.4%; Leather and Leather Products 0.2%. Petroleum, Coal Products and Nuclear Fuels took 3.5% while growing 14.8% a year and slowing (-19.20 pp) — a smaller slice of a faster-growing total, not a retreat.
insights.implication: Shares of new lending move far faster than shares of the book, so this is the earlier read of the two. It says where the money went, not why — and a falling share alongside rising growth means the others grew faster, not that this one shrank.

inferences: Every sector's industry credit is compared with the same month a year earlier, and each one's share of the total increase is taken.
Infrastructure accounts for 19.0% of the increase.
All sectors moved the same way this window, so the shares of the net increase are bounded and sum to a hundred.
